## Detailed entries

### Bourbonnais

- **Type:** Village
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** Village Board of Trustees passed the moratorium ordinance by a 4-0 vote (two trustees absent) at its Monday, June 15, 2026 meeting, after the Economic and Community Development Committee unanimously recommended it on June 10, 2026.
- **Date field:** `2026-06-15` (exact)
- **Duration:** Temporary moratorium on data centers within the village; a June 16, 2026 report gave January 31, 2027 as the end date. A retained pre-meeting ordinance version also provided for earlier termination by a majority vote and specified 4:30 p.m.; the final enacted text has not been located.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `il-bourbonnais-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Village of Bourbonnais ordinance establishing a data center moratorium. A retained pre-meeting version is numbered 26-2552; the final enacted text and its number have not been independently verified. The original dataset described this as the first such measure by a Kankakee County local government.
- **What prompted it:** Resident concern/social-media rumors about a data center locating in the village; trustees wanted legal groundwork in place to keep data centers out of village boundaries (the moratorium does not apply outside them).
- **Affected projects:** No specific project named; officials said the moratorium was prompted by rumors rather than a known proposal.
- **Status notes:** Active as of 2026-09-23; runs through January 31, 2027 per the ordinance.
- **Outcome:** Temporary fix giving officials time to protect the village from future data centers.

### Catlin

- **Type:** Village
- **Status:** ⚪ Replaced
- **Recorded date:** October 7, 2025 (Catlin Village Council passed a moratorium on new solar energy projects Tuesday evening, per Vermilion County First, 2025-10-09); the Village's own public statement confirms the ordinance runs through April 30, 2026 as first adopted, before later extensions.
- **Date field:** `2025-10-07` (exact)
- **Duration:** The Village Council passed a solar-project moratorium on October 7, 2025, initially through April 30, 2026; the board later extended the solar-farm moratorium in approximately 30-day increments while developing wind and solar zoning. A report describes an extension to August 31, 2026, and a September 1 report says the prior moratorium expired August 31. The village identifies Wind and Solar Ordinance 799 as approved August 27, 2026.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** solar, wind
- **Record ID:** `il-catlin-undated`
- **Authority and source:** An ordinance adopting a solar-development moratorium was reported passed October 7, 2025; the Village Board later extended the moratorium (instrument numbers not established). The village identifies Ordinance No. 799, Wind and Solar Energy Ordinance, as approved August 27, 2026.
- **What prompted it:** Earthrise Energy's proposed 1,400-acre solar-farm project along Catlin-Tilton Road; the village wanted time to draft zoning language addressing setbacks, screening, and water testing for industrial-scale solar and wind projects before acting on the application.
- **Affected projects:** Earthrise Energy's proposed 1,400-acre solar farm along Catlin-Tilton Road (Tilton Solar project).
- **Status notes:** The prior solar-farm moratorium expired August 31, 2026, according to a September 1 report. The village identifies a wind and solar ordinance approved August 27, and the report says applications could be submitted from September 1.
- **Outcome:** The moratorium was replaced by a permanent solar/wind zoning ordinance approved by the Village Council in late August 2026, which now governs special-use applications for wind and solar projects (including annual water testing for private wells within 500 feet of a project boundary).

### City of Aurora

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** ⚪ Replaced
- **Recorded date:** 2025-09-25
- **Date field:** `2025-09-25` (exact)
- **Duration:** 180 days, with one-time 30-day extension invoked before final ordinance adoption
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `il-aurora-2025`
- **Authority and source:** Ordinance O25-064
- **What prompted it:** Rapid expansion of data centers in northern Illinois; existing code classified data centers as warehouses; city cited neighborhood complaints, noise, emissions, high energy and water use, stormwater, utility demand, infrastructure strain, and fiscal impacts.
- **Affected projects:** New data center and warehouse developments, subject to carve-outs for previously filed entitlement applications, existing data center remodels, routine maintenance, and public safety facilities. Aurora reported five data centers in city limits and five more in development when it adopted the permanent rules.
- **Status notes:** Replaced
- **Outcome:** City Council approved new rules on 2026-03-24, described by the city as adopted on 2026-03-25. New data centers are conditional uses requiring public hearing, public notice, City Council approval, development agreement, water study and plan, energy plan, sound study and plan, noise and vibration limits, energy and water limits, no evaporative cooling, no modular nuclear, annual energy and water reporting, annual noise testing, and either on-site renewables or battery storage or alternative compliance.

- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** Lake County Board approved the moratorium ordinance on Tuesday, 2026-09-08, following a unanimous recommendation from the Zoning Board of Appeals on Aug. 18, 2026 and unanimous approval by the Planning, Building, Zoning and Environment Committee on Sept. 2, 2026.
- **Date field:** `2026-09-08` (exact)

- **What prompted it:** Lake County's Unified Development Ordinance does not specifically define or regulate data centers; the County received more than 1,200 online public comments and hundreds of in-person attendees on the issue before adopting the pause.

### Logan County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🔴 Rescinded
- **Recorded date:** County Board approved a 60-day moratorium 9-2 on 2026-02-24; after it lapsed, the Board approved a 12-month moratorium 6-4 on 2026-05-19. The May 19 moratorium was declared procedurally invalid by the State's Attorney on 2026-06-18 for skipping the required Zoning Board of Appeals advisory review and public hearings.
- **Date field:** `2026-05-19` (exact)

As of an Aug. 4, 2026 committee meeting, the Board was drafting a replacement moratorium (covering data centers exceeding 100 MW) and had submitted it to the State's Attorney for review; as of a Sept. 17-18, 2026 report, the Board had not adopted a new moratorium and was instead advancing 18 amendments to its permanent data-center zoning ordinance.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `il-logan-county-2026`
- **Authority and source:** 12-month moratorium approved by County Board vote 2026-05-19; declared invalid by Logan County State's Attorney Bradley Hauge on 2026-06-18 because it was not referred to the Zoning Board of Appeals for advisory review or subjected to public hearings before final passage, as required by county procedure.
- **What prompted it:** Response to Hut 8 Corp.'s proposed ~500 MW 'Logan Prairie' data center near Latham; residents sought time to study the project and adopt safeguards before the county acted on Hut 8's land-use application.
- **Affected projects:** Hut 8 Corp.'s proposed 'Logan Prairie Data Center' (~500 MW, originally on ~250 acres, later refiled for 720 acres) near Latham, IL; a ~$5B project. Hut 8 has also been in talks with the Village of Latham about possible annexation, which could remove the site from county zoning jurisdiction.
- **Status notes:** The earlier dataset recorded the measure as not in force as of 2026-09-23; its later reporting was not independently reviewed in this pass. The May 19, 2026 moratorium was declared procedurally invalid by the State’s Attorney on 2026-06-18, and the State's Attorney directed the zoning office to accept Hut 8's rezoning application (deemed complete June 29, 2026); Hut 8 has since filed a further rezoning application for a 720-acre site. As of Aug. 4, 2026, the Board's Zoning and Economic Development Committee was drafting a replacement moratorium (targeting data centers over 100 MW) and submitted it to the State's Attorney for review, but no adoption had been reported by Sept. 17-18, 2026; that most recent reporting instead describes the Board advancing 18 amendments to its permanent data-center zoning ordinance (height cap, setbacks, a faster environmental-discharge cure period), separate from any new moratorium.
- **Outcome:** The county's attempt to pause data-center applications while it developed permanent zoning was defeated on procedural grounds; as of this research pass the county had not re-adopted a valid moratorium and was instead pursuing amendments to a permanent data-center zoning ordinance while Hut 8's rezoning application proceeds.

### HB3574 (Procurement-Data Residency)

- **Policy ID:** `il-hb3574-procurement-data-residency`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Justin Slaughter and House co-sponsors; Senate sponsors Lakesia Collins and Doris Turner; D
- **Status:** Passed House 114-1-0 on 2025-04-10; arrived in Senate, assigned to Executive Committee, deadline extended, then re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2025-06-02. No later action appears in the history observed 2026-11-05.
- **Provisions:** Engrossed proposal requires U.S. processing, storage and disposal of defined state data under covered storage contracts unless the chief procurement officer authorizes otherwise, with exclusions including primarily telecommunications contracts. Credits earned after qualifying contract completion favor Illinois and qualified-area storage for future bids; qualifying data-center RFPs also receive location preference points.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; state_agency
- **Legal effect:** proposed
- **Effective date:** —

### HB4319 (Data Center-Property Rights)

- **Policy ID:** `il-hb4319-data-center-property-rights`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Jed Davis; R
- **Status:** Filed 2026-01-07; first reading and referred to House Rules Committee 2026-01-14. No later action appears in the history observed 2026-11-05.
- **Provisions:** Introduced proposal creates a compensation framework for qualifying property within 1,000 feet of a data center when construction or operation materially and proximately causes specified measurable harm, including property-value or business-revenue loss and qualifying adverse impacts. It provides appraisal and civil-remedy procedures and limits concurrent home-rule powers; proximity alone does not establish compensation eligibility.

### SB0094 (Data Centers-Foreign Ownership)

- **Policy ID:** `il-sb0094-data-centers-foreign-ownership`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Sue Rezin; co-sponsors Sally J. Turner and Terri Bryant; R
- **Status:** Referred to Senate Assignments Committee 2025-01-17; co-sponsors added 2025-04-03. No later action appears in the history observed 2026-11-05.
- **Provisions:** Introduced Data Center Construction by Foreign Adversaries Act would bar a foreign company from constructing or causing construction of a data center unless ICC, IPA and DCEO jointly study its energy consumption and certify to the Governor and General Assembly that estimated energy use is a self-generated load and does not affect the PJM or MISO load supply. A foreign company is one at least 51% owned by a foreign adversary or headquartered in a country whose government is a foreign adversary, as defined by reference to 15 CFR 791.2.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; statewide
- **Legal effect:** proposed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://www.ilga.gov/Legislation/BillStatus?DocNum=94&DocTypeID=SB&GAID=18&SessionID=114>)

### SB4004 (Aquifer Protection Act)

- **Policy ID:** `il-sb4004-aquifer-protection-act`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Chapin Rose; R
- **Status:** To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-25; Rule 2-10 deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; Senate Committee Amendment No. 1 filed 2026-05-05; bill and amendment re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22; co-sponsors added through 2026-09-02 (Latest sponsor-action date is distinct from the last substantive re-referral.) Retained official history observed 2026-11-07; later disposition not independently established.
- **Provisions:** As introduced, proposes a blanket Mahomet Aquifer data-center water prohibition and a January 1, 2028 transition for existing facilities. The introduced synopsis names January 1, 2027, while introduced section 15 contains no such start date; no date is assigned from that discrepancy. Filed Senate Committee Amendment No. 1 proposes replacing the bill with water-resource plans, Illinois State Water Survey impact reports, an adverse-resource-impact-dependent Mahomet withdrawal prohibition, quarterly DNR reporting, scarcity plans and water-use NDA restrictions. Existing centers would submit plans within six months; January 1, 2028 withdrawal cessation depends on an adverse-impact determination. The amendment is recorded filed/re-referred, not adopted; neither proposal is represented as current law.
- **Mechanism / scope:** permitting_restriction; statewide
- **Legal effect:** proposed
